problems.title: Common-prediction accuracy cannot exceed purity
claim: The proposed method reports ACC/PUR \((99.67,99.64)\) on BDGP and \((98.66,98.43)\) on Handwritten; numerous baseline pairs also have ACC above purity.
analysis: For contingency counts \(C_{kj}\ge0\), each matching term \(C_{k,\pi(k)}\le\max_jC_{kj}\). Summing and maximizing proves \(\mathrm{ACC}\le\mathrm{PUR}\), including unequal class/cluster counts via zero padding. The inequality survives matched nonnegative-weight averaging and separate maxima over the same run collection. Ordinary common rounding preserves it; even independent \(0.005\)-percentage-point errors cannot explain gaps \(0.03\) and \(0.23\). The current metric functions implement these definitions. Different sample/run collections or nonstandard aggregation could explain coexistence only with an explicit different protocol; transcription remains possible.
result: The table cannot currently be read as mutually consistent metrics from common predictions under its stated definitions. The wrong cell or underlying cause is not identified, and no fabrication or corrected true accuracy is inferred.
repair: Recover sample IDs, true/predicted labels, run IDs and aggregation weights; compute both metrics on each common prediction vector and regenerate affected tables. The ordering is necessary, not sufficient, for experimental validity.

problems.title: Zeroing rejected scores does not exclude their agents
claim: A failed confidence threshold sets an agent’s raw score to zero before softmax. Its resulting numerator is \(e^0=1\), so it remains in the mixture.
analysis: With \(2\) views, \(2\) samples, \(2\) clusters and threshold \(0.7\), let the only accepted agent predict rows \((0.71,0.29),(0.29,0.71)\); each of three rejected agents predicts \((0.31,0.69),(0.69,0.31)\). Feature norms \(0.01\) give raw scores \((0.0071,0,0,0)\). Softmax assigns total rejected mass approximately \(0.7486663884\); the first fused row is approximately \[(0.4105334446,0.5894665554)\], reversing the accepted decision, with the second reversed symmetrically. All rows are valid positive probabilities. This refutes strict exclusion, while a deliberate softer downweighting interpretation remains legitimate.
result: The printed rule does not implement strict rejection and can let rejected agents determine the result. This is a formula-level witness conditional on a valid routing threshold, without any LLM call or benchmark claim.
repair: For nonempty accepted set \(A\), normalize \(w_a=\mathbf1_{a\in A}e^{r_a-r_*}/\sum_{b\in A}e^{r_b-r_*}\). This gives zero rejected weight and unit mass. If all agents fail, explicitly abstain or declare a relaxed-threshold fallback.

problems.title: The core detaches both contrastive encoder losses
claim: The trainer obtains all view features through an accessor using no-gradient recording, then constructs feature and frequency contrastive terms exclusively from those returned features.
analysis: No recorded derivative connects these features back to encoder parameters. The frequency module’s FFT/amplitude/distance operations have no trainable parameter that recreates that missing edge, so adding either loss to another differentiable term cannot supply its intended encoder derivative. Other direct encoder calls remain differentiable, so this does not disable all training. The historical CPU witness reports finite contrastive losses and restored nonzero gradients under a connected-accessor control; those author-method executions were not rerun in this pass.
result: The archived official core cannot realize the stated encoder optimization from these two terms along the inspected path. Full experiment implementation identity and benchmark effects remain unknown.
repair: Use a training accessor with gradient recording enabled for these losses, keeping inference-only suppression separate. Verify optimizer membership and the connected derivative; no full retrained replacement is certified.

problems.impact_rationale: This is an exact gradient-path defect in supplied core code; the supplement is not established as the complete historical training system.
